stem: In an infant with bronchiolitis, which one of the following organisms is the most likely cause?
explanation: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in infants. It typically presents with coryzal symptoms, wheeze, crackles, and respiratory distress in a young infant.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The question describes a classic infant bronchiolitis presentation, for which RSV is the most likely pathogen.

optionExplanations.A: Parainfluenza viruses can cause croup and other respiratory infections, but they are not the commonest cause of bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.B: Rhinovirus can cause bronchiolitis and wheezing illnesses, but RSV is more likely in this classic presentation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: RSV is the most common cause of bronchiolitis in infants.
optionExplanations.D: Adenovirus may cause lower respiratory tract infection, but it is less commonly the cause of bronchiolitis than RSV.
optionExplanations.E: Human metapneumovirus can cause bronchiolitis, but RSV remains the most likely organism overall.

Instructions

The following nine questions refer to Patrick’s clinical scenario.

Clinical scenario 1 - Patrick

Patrick, a six month old infant, is brought to the emergency department with wheezing and respiratory distress. On examination he has severe chest wall retractions, grunting and is pale. His vital signs are:

RR 80/min, HR 190/min, temperature 38.0’C, SaO2 80% in room air.

The accompanying table has the normal ranges indicated in the 2010 NSW Health Standard Paediatric Observation Chart, SPOC.

Patrick has wheeze and crackles throughout his chest. There is a history of having been snuffly with a cough for the last two days. The entire family has a cold.
